questions.knowledgeNote: sin = 1 only at the top of the principal arc: pi/2.
questions.question: Q1(a). Evaluate sin-1(1) without using tables.
questions.solution: sin-1(1) is the angle t in [-pi/2, pi/2] with sint = 1, i.e. t = pi/2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q1(a); book p167 = PDF p194 (600-dpi crop + OCR read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Negative arguments give negative principal values for sin-1.
questions.question: Q1(b). Evaluate sin-1(-1/2) without using tables.
questions.solution: sin-1(-1/2) is t in [-pi/2, pi/2] with sint = -1/2, i.e. t = -pi/6. (Stacked fraction resolved at 600dpi: OCR reads the argument as -1/2.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q1(b); book p167 = PDF p194 (600-dpi crop + OCR read)

questions.knowledgeNote: cos-1 of a negative number lands in QII: here 120 degrees.
questions.question: Q1(c). Evaluate cos-1(-1/2) without using tables.
questions.solution: cos-1(-1/2) is t in [0, pi] with cost = -1/2, i.e. t = 2pi/3. (Direct 600-dpi read of the stacked argument gives numerator 1 over denominator 2, i.e. -1/2, confirmed at 0.99/1.00 confidence.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q1(c); book p167 = PDF p194 (600-dpi crop + OCR read)

questions.knowledgeNote: tan = 1 at the first-quadrant standard angle pi/4.
questions.question: Q1(d). Evaluate tan-1(1) without using tables.
questions.solution: tan-1(1) is t in (-pi/2, pi/2) with tant = 1, i.e. t = pi/4.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q1(d); book p167 = PDF p194 (600-dpi crop + OCR read)

questions.knowledgeNote: arccot ranges over (0, pi): cot = -1 gives 3pi/4, not -pi/4.
questions.question: Q1(e). Evaluate arccot(-1) without using tables.
questions.solution: arccot(-1) is t in (0, pi) with cott = -1, i.e. t = 3pi/4.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q1(e); book p167 = PDF p194 (600-dpi crop + OCR read)

questions.knowledgeNote: tan = -1/sqrt(3) is the negative of the 30-degree slope.
questions.question: Q1(f). Evaluate arctan(-1/sqrt(3)) without using tables.
questions.solution: arctan(-1/sqrt(3)) is t in (-pi/2, pi/2) with tant = -1/sqrt(3), i.e. t = -pi/6. (The sqrt(3) confirmed by a V3 glyph read in the 600-dpi crop.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q1(f); book p167 = PDF p194 (600-dpi crop + OCR read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Draw the right triangle with opposite x, adjacent 1: hypotenuse sqrt(1+x^2).
questions.question: Q2(a). Express cos(tan-1x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put t = tan-1x, so t is in (-pi/2, pi/2) and tant = x. Then cost = 1/sqrt(1+tan^2t) = 1/sqrt(1+x^2), positive since cost > 0 on (-pi/2, pi/2). Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 1/sqrt(1+x^2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(a); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.96); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Same triangle read from the cot side: adjacent x, opposite 1.
questions.question: Q2(b). Express sin(cot-1x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put p = cot-1x, so p is in (0, pi) and cotp = x. Then sinp = 1/sqrt(1+cot^2p) = 1/sqrt(1+x^2), positive since sinp > 0 on (0, pi). Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 1/sqrt(1+x^2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(b); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.90); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: tan and arccot are reciprocal functions: tan(arccot x) = 1/x.
questions.question: Q2(c). Express tan(arccot x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put p = arccot x, so cotp = x with x != 0. Then tanp = 1/cotp = 1/x. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 1/x (x != 0).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(c); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.94); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cos is non-negative on the whole sin-1 range, so no sign choice.
questions.question: Q2(d). Express cos(sin-1x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put t = sin-1x, so t is in [-pi/2, pi/2] and sint = x. Then cost = +sqrt(1-sin^2t) = sqrt(1-x^2), taking the non-negative root since cost >= 0 there. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): sqrt(1-x^2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(d); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.97); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Double-angle in tan form: tan2t = 2tant/(1-tan^2t) with tant = x.
questions.question: Q2(e). Express tan(2tan-1x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put t = tan-1x so tant = x. Then tan2t = 2tant/(1-tan^2t) = 2x/(1-x^2), valid for x != +-1. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 2x/(1-x^2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(e); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.96); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: sin2t via tan: 2tant/(1+tan^2t) - denominator never zero.
questions.question: Q2(f). Express sin(2tan-1x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put t = tan-1x so tant = x. Then sin2t = 2tant/(1+tan^2t) = 2x/(1+x^2). Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 2x/(1+x^2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(f); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.93); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cos2p from cot: (cot^2p-1)/(cot^2p+1) - test x = 1 gives cos(pi/2) = 0.
questions.question: Q2(g). Express cos(2cot-1x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put p = cot-1x so cotp = x. Then cos2p = (cot^2p-1)/(cot^2p+1) = (x^2-1)/(x^2+1). Check x = 1: cos(2.pi/4) = cos(pi/2) = 0 and (1-1)/(1+1) = 0. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): (x^2-1)/(x^2+1).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(g); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.95); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cot2p from cot: (cot^2p-1)/(2cotp) - test x = 1 gives cot(pi/2) = 0.
questions.question: Q2(h). Express cot(2arccot x) in terms of x.
questions.solution: Put p = arccot x so cotp = x with x != 0. Then cot2p = (cot^2p-1)/(2cotp) = (x^2-1)/(2x). Check x = 1: cot(2.pi/4) = 0 and (1-1)/2 = 0. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): (x^2-1)/(2x).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q2(h); book p167 = PDF p194 (OCR conf 0.97); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: 3-4-5 triangle: cos = 3/5 forces sin = 4/5.
questions.question: Q3(a). Evaluate sin(cos-1(3/5)).
questions.solution: Let t = cos-1(3/5), so cost = 3/5 with t in [0, pi] and hence sint >= 0. Then sint = sqrt(1-9/25) = 4/5. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 4/5. (Scan shows sin(cos-1(3/...)) with the denominator lost; the value 3/5 is forced by the key 4/5.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q3(a); book p167 = PDF p194 (statement reconstructed: 3/5 forced by the key 4/5); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: Principal-value round trip: cos undoes arccos exactly.
questions.question: Q3(b). Evaluate cos(arccos(2/3)).
questions.solution: arccos(2/3) lies in [0, pi], the exact range on which cos inverts arccos, so cos(arccos(2/3)) = 2/3. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 2/3. (Scan shows cos(arccos(...3)) with the numerator lost; the value 2/3 is forced by the key.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q3(b); book p167 = PDF p194 (statement reconstructed: 2/3 forced by the key); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: arctan undoes tan only inside (-pi/2, pi/2): pi/6 qualifies.
questions.question: Q3(c). Evaluate arctan(tan(pi/6)).
questions.solution: pi/6 lies in (-pi/2, pi/2), so arctan(tan(pi/6)) = pi/6. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): pi/6.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q3(c); book p167 = PDF p194 (statement via 600-dpi crop: the argument reads as pi/6); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: 3-4-5 triangle read from the tan side: tant = 3/4 forces sint = 3/5.
questions.question: Q3(d). Evaluate sin(tan-1(3/4)).
questions.solution: Let t = tan-1(3/4), acute with tant = 3/4. Then sint = 3/5 (opposite 3, hypotenuse 5). Matches the printed Answers key (p169): 3/5.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q3(d); book p167 = PDF p194 (statement via 600-dpi crop: tan-1(3/4) read); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: cos-1(1/2) is exactly 60 degrees, so double it before taking sin.
questions.question: Q3(e). Evaluate sin(2cos-1(1/2)).
questions.solution: cos-1(1/2) = pi/3, so sin(2.pi/3) = sin(120deg) = sqrt(3)/2. Matches the printed Answers key (p169): sqrt(3)/2. (The stacked 1/2 resolved at 600dpi: fraction bar read as 1-2 at 0.85 confidence.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.5 Ex 5.1 Q3(e); book p167 = PDF p194 (statement via 600-dpi argument crop); matches key

questions.knowledgeNote: 2cos(pi/3) = 1, and sin-1(1) = pi/2: collapse the inside first.
questions.question: Q3(f). Evaluate sin-1(2cos(pi/3)).
questions.solution: 2cos(pi/3) = 2.(1/2) = 1, so sin-1(1) = pi/2. (This key row is illegible in the key scan; verified by direct substitution instead.)
